events.title: Early Settlement
events.description: Migrants from India and Sri Lanka settled in Maldives islands. Early inhabitants practiced Buddhism and Hinduism.

events.title: Buddhist Period
events.description: Maldives became Buddhist nation, closely connected with Sri Lankan Buddhist culture. Many Buddhist ruins still exist today.

events.title: Conversion to Islam
events.description: Moroccan traveler (legend) or Arab merchants brought Islam, Maldivian king and people converted to Islam. Islam became state religion to this day.

events.title: Sultanate Period
events.description: Maldives ruled by hereditary sultans, becoming important transit point in Indian Ocean trade. Famous for cowrie shell currency trade.

events.title: Portuguese Occupation
events.description: Portugal occupied Maldives for 15 years. But Maldivians led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu rebelled and expelled Portuguese. Thakurufaanu became national hero.

events.title: British Protectorate
events.description: Maldives became British protectorate. Britain controlled foreign affairs and defense, but internal affairs governed by sultan autonomously.

events.title: First Constitution
events.description: Maldives promulgated first constitution, introducing electoral system. But sultanate system remained.

events.title: First Republic (Short-lived)
events.description: Maldives abolished sultanate, establishing republic. But only 8 months later, monarchy was restored.

events.title: Maldives Independence
events.description: Maldives gained independence from British protection, becoming an independent nation. However, sultanate system remained. July 26 became Independence Day.

events.title: Second Republic Established
events.description: Referendum abolished sultanate system, Maldives became republic. Ibrahim Nasir elected as first president.

events.title: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom Takes Power
events.description: Gayoom elected president, beginning 30-year rule (1978-2008). He promoted modernization and tourism development but practiced authoritarian rule.

events.title: Tourism Boom
events.description: Maldives vigorously developed luxury resort tourism, utilizing beautiful coral reefs and beaches. Tourism became economic pillar, Maldives became world-class vacation destination.

events.title: Coup Attempt
events.description: Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries attempted to overthrow Gayoom government. India intervened at request, suppressing coup.

events.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.description: Indonesian earthquake triggered tsunami hitting Maldives, killing about 100, affecting 1/3 of population. As a low-lying atoll nation, Maldives is extremely vulnerable to sea-level rise threats.

events.title: Democracy Movement
events.description: People demanded democratic reforms, opposing Gayoom's long-term autocracy. Under international pressure, government began democratization reforms.

events.title: New Constitution and Democratic Elections
events.description: Maldives promulgated new constitution, implementing multi-party democracy. In first democratic election, Mohamed Nasheed defeated Gayoom, ending 30-year rule.

events.title: Underwater Cabinet Meeting
events.description: President Nasheed and cabinet held cabinet meeting underwater in diving equipment, calling for international attention to climate change and sea-level rise threats to Maldives. This became global news headlines.

events.title: Nasheed Forced to Resign
events.description: Under pressure from police and military, President Nasheed was forced to resign. He called it a coup, internationally controversial. Vice President Waheed took over.

events.title: Abdulla Yameen Elected
events.description: Abdulla Yameen, brother of former dictator Gayoom, elected president. He pursued pro-China policy, democracy regressed.

events.title: Nasheed Sentenced to Prison
events.description: Former President Nasheed sentenced to 13 years imprisonment on terrorism charges. International community condemned this as political persecution.

events.title: Authoritarian Rule and Chinese Investment
events.description: Yameen government suppressed opposition, arrested judges and politicians. Meanwhile heavily introduced Chinese investment, joined Belt and Road, resulting in massive debt.

events.title: Ibrahim Solih Elected
events.description: Opposition candidate Solih defeated Yameen in election, achieving regime change. Democracy restored, Nasheed and other political prisoners released.

events.title: Climate Change Threat
events.description: Maldives is the world's lowest-lying country (average elevation only 1.5 meters), sea-level rise is an existential threat. Government calls for international community to address climate change and considers purchasing foreign land as 'backup homeland.'

events.title: Mohamed Muizzu Elected
events.description: Pro-China candidate Muizzu elected president, demanding Indian troops withdrawal. Maldives became focus in geopolitical competition between China and India.

events.title: Maldivian Kingdom Established
events.description: Maldives established a unified Buddhist kingdom, maintaining close cultural ties with Sri Lanka. Maldives became an important transit point in Indian Ocean trade.

events.title: Whole Island Converts to Islam
events.description: Sultan Muhammad ibn Abdullah established Islam as state religion, all Buddhist temples converted to mosques. This marked fundamental cultural transformation of Maldives.

events.title: Ibn Battuta's Visit
events.description: Famous Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta visited Maldives and served as judge. His travelogue detailed Maldivian society, culture and trade.

events.title: Cowrie Shell Currency Trade Flourishes
events.description: Maldivian cowrie shells became important currency in parts of Africa and Asia. Shell trade brought enormous wealth to Maldives.

events.title: Portuguese Expulsion
events.description: Muhammad Thakurufaanu led Maldivian people to expel Portuguese occupiers after 15 years, restoring independence. He became national hero, honored as Sultan.

events.title: Dutch and French Influence
events.description: Dutch and French successively attempted to control Maldivian trade, but Maldivian sultans successfully maintained independence, allowing only limited trade relations.

events.title: Short-lived Republic Experiment
events.description: Maldives briefly abolished sultanate system, establishing republic. But less than a year later monarchy was restored.

events.title: British Protectorate Agreement
events.description: Maldives signed formal protectorate agreement with Britain. Britain guaranteed Maldives against foreign aggression but didn't interfere in internal affairs. Annual subsidy increased.

events.title: Traditional Society Maintained
events.description: Under British protection, Maldives maintained traditional sultan rule and Islamic social structure. Modernization progressed slowly, basically maintaining medieval lifestyle.

events.title: British Base During WWII
events.description: During WWII, Britain established air force base on Gan Island, Maldives, protecting Indian Ocean routes. Maldives first encountered large-scale modern military facilities.

events.title: First Republic Experiment
events.description: Amin Didi led republican movement, abolishing sultanate system. But reforms too radical, triggering conservative opposition. Monarchy restored after 8 months.

events.title: Gan Base Controversy
events.description: British extension of Gan base lease sparked Maldivian discontent. Sultanate negotiated with Britain over base issues, demanding more compensation.

events.title: Southern Rebellion
events.description: Southern atolls of Maldives declared independence with British support, forming 'United Suvadive Republic.' Government suppressed rebellion in 1963, restoring unity.

events.title: British Withdrawal from Gan Base
events.description: Britain withdrew from Gan air force base. Maldives gained control of base, later developed into resort island.

events.title: Luxury Resort Model Established
events.description: Maldives established unique 'one island, one hotel' resort model. Luxury overwater bungalows and private vacation experiences attracted wealthy tourists globally.

events.title: Joined SAARC
events.description: Maldives became founding member of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), strengthening ties with South Asian countries.

events.title: Coup Details
events.description: Tamil mercenary coup attempted to overthrow President Gayoom. India dispatched 1600 paratroopers within 24 hours (Operation Cactus), quickly suppressing rebellion, saving Maldivian democratic government.

events.title: Commonwealth Secretariat Meeting
events.description: Maldivian capital Malé hosted Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, the largest international event in Maldivian history, enhancing international status.

events.title: Tourism Impact After 9/11
events.description: After 9/11 global tourism declined, Maldives as highly tourism-dependent country was impacted. Government strengthened security measures to restore tourist confidence.

events.title: Prison Riot
events.description: Serious riot occurred in Malé prison, prisoners took hostages. Event exposed Maldivian prison system problems and Gayoom government's authoritarian rule.

events.title: Reconstruction and International Aid
events.description: After tsunami, international community provided substantial aid. Maldives rebuilt infrastructure but became more aware of climate change vulnerability.

events.title: Constitutional Reform
events.description: Under domestic and international pressure, Gayoom government agreed to constitutional reforms, allowing multiparty system and presidential term limits. Paved way for 2008 democratic election.

events.title: Climate Change Initiative
events.description: Nasheed government announced Maldives would achieve carbon neutrality within 10 years, becoming global climate change leadership.

events.title: Yameen's Dictatorship
events.description: President Yameen declared state of emergency, arrested Supreme Court judges, suppressed protests. Maldivian democracy severely regressed, called 'dictatorship in Indian Ocean.'

events.title: Anti-Corruption Campaign
events.description: Solih government launched large-scale anti-corruption investigation, tracking Yameen government's corruption cases. Estimated billions of dollars embezzled.

events.title: India-Maldives Tensions
events.description: Muizzu government demanded India withdraw 75 military personnel stationed in Maldives. India-Maldives relations cooled, Maldives turning toward China.
